newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain urges fund caution in new derivatives trade.
newsitem.headline: Spain urges fund caution in new derivatives trade.

text.p: Spain's national stock market commission (CNMV) said on Monday investment funds would be allowed to trade in derivatives but urged increased control and vigilance over fund managers using the high-risk instruments.

"This greater investment freedom for the funds comes accompanied by greater levels of demand for responsibility in their management because it also incorporates a greater level of exposure to risk," CNMV president Juan Fernandez-Armesto told a seminar on Spain's derivatives markets.
The CNMV is to approve a circular on Tuesday spelling out initial steps investment funds should take in derivatives trade.

"A fund manager will not be able to invest in derivatives without the explicit approval of its board," Armesto said, adding that board members should also ensure the separation of the management, accounting and control functions and clearly define the risk limits for each fund.

A ministerial order on June 10 gave approval for investment funds to use derivatives and OTC contracts up to a limit of 10 percent of the fund capital in options. The order also gave the CNMV wide authority to change the limits or instruments.
Arnesto said the CNMV would approve a second circular before the end of the year and would, depending on the results to then, either liberalise or toughen regulations to protect investors.
